content:
Looking at each shape, I can tile A, B, C, and E with five T‑tetrominoes (constructible placements exist for each). For shape D, however, the narrow vertical column (highlighted in red) forces contradictions: the cell at the bottom of that column has only one neighbor, forcing one T-piece to occupy the column cells plus a specific side square; this in turn forces a second T-piece onto the top of the column. After these forced placements, a square sticking out to the right of the column becomes isolated and cannot be covered by any whole piece. Hence D cannot be tiled by exactly 5 T-pieces.

\boxed{D}
